baselines.baryonic: training-only affine calibration of a fixed exponential Rc disk plus spherical Sersic bulge light model with one fixed stellar mass-to-light proxy
baselines.flexible_nuisance: fixed ridge regression on smooth log baryonic speed, log radius, radius powers, log acceleration, mass, surface brightness, inclination, morphology, bulge fraction, bar, disk break, seeing resolution, and predeclared interactions, with no periodic basis

counterexamples_and_limitations: Rc light with a fixed stellar mass-to-light proxy omits resolved atomic, molecular, ionized-gas, remnant, and dust mass.
H-alpha traces ionized gas, not the speed of every star, and noncircular motions can enter both sides of a curve.
The exponential disk plus spherical Sersic bulge approximation is an intentionally fixed baryonic-light control, not a precision mass model.
A periodic residual may expose photometric structure, sampling, or instrument systematics rather than gravity.

A positive exploration result becomes at most a phenomenon lead; an unchanged independent replication is required before a paper claim, and later lensing, cluster, local, stability, and cosmology gates are required for a gravity claim.

discovery_policy.partial_result_track: Retain preregistered regime-specific periodic structure as a scoped replication hypothesis when it clears its frozen effect and null thresholds, without calling it universal or a paper result.
discovery_policy.phenomenon_publication_track: Independently retain any reproducible common radial, clock, log-scale, or baryon-coupled periodic relation that beats the strongest ordinary controls on its measured domain, even if it is not gravity or does not solve missing mass.
discovery_policy.universal_gravity_track: Require one unchanged periodic family with a common wavelength and phase rule to beat baryonic and flexible smooth controls across held-out galaxies, both kinematic sides, radial halves, mass halves, surface-brightness halves, selection-aware nulls, and local limits.

exact_next_action: Preserve every periodic family and scoped result under the equal-viability two-track policy; require unchanged independent replication before any paper claim; advance to Item 29 nonlinear self-interaction without privileging or pruning age, periodicity, or any other distinct mechanism.

frozen_boundary.implementation_correction_scope: First, use the documented GHASP VI VizieR column label NBins and the GHASP VII label Nbins for the same frozen minimum-velocity-bin field. VizieR silently omitted the case-mismatched GHASP VI column, causing every otherwise valid GHASP VI row to fail integer parsing. Requery only the same 49 already-authorized exploration identities. Second, correct the receipt's prose-only Item 29 label from dimensional leakage to the stable roadmap's nonlinear self-interaction. Change no identity, role, fold, response value, threshold, radius grid, formula, candidate, baseline, result metric, confirmation boundary, or promotion gate.
frozen_boundary.response_access_incident: The first post-freeze acquisition queried exactly the 49 authorized exploration identities and zero confirmations. GHASP VI returned its documented NBins column only when requested with an uppercase B, whereas the frozen generic query requested the GHASP VII spelling Nbins; VizieR silently omitted the unknown field. Thirty-five GHASP VI curves therefore failed parsing before evaluation. The correction requeries only those same 49 exploration identities using the catalog-specific schema alias and preserves every scientific boundary.

external_constraints.scope: Independent total-light, disk, bulge, bar, inclination, size, and surface-brightness predictors.

external_constraints.scope: Known oscillatory gravitational behavior in linearized higher- and infinite-derivative gravity; spatial oscillations themselves are not historically new.

external_constraints.scope: Known connection between logarithmic oscillations, discrete scale invariance, and beyond-Einstein gravity.

external_constraints.label: Burrage and Dombrowski, local time variation of G
external_constraints.scope: Local-measurement constraints and screening caveats for time-dependent gravitational couplings.

external_constraints.label: McGaugh, Lelli, and Schombert, radial acceleration relation
external_constraints.scope: Strong smooth baryon-acceleration comparator and warning that baryonic features can track rotation-curve features without periodic gravity.

theory_and_equivalence_audit.local_limit: The same low-acceleration window is evaluated at one AU using Solar acceleration; admitted cells must remain below the frozen fractional-response bound.

niche_rules.baryonic_orbital_clock: theta=2*pi*t_bar_myr/T_myr+phi, where t_bar is computed only from radius and the frozen baryonic-light prediction

prior_equivalence: A sinusoidal correction is a known mathematical basis and is not itself a new formula.
Spatial oscillations overlap known higher-derivative and nonlocal gravitational ripple families.
The Item 25 oscillatory cosmic-history equation is retained as an equivalence comparator but is not retuned here; GHASP has no useful redshift-history leverage.
Baryonic orbital-clock and phase-coupled forms are potentially distinct syntheses only, not evidence of historical novelty.
Spiral arms, bars, disk breaks, beam smearing, interpolation, asymmetric drift, and baryonic profile features are ordinary non-gravitational or standard-gravity explanations.
theory_and_equivalence_audit.response_rule: At every resolved radius, log10(v)=log10(v_baryonic calibrated on training galaxies)+A*s*W(g_bar)*E(r/h)*(sin(theta)+q2*sin(2*theta))/(2 ln 10), with one universal cell and no galaxy-specific periodic parameter.
theory_and_equivalence_audit.stability_limit: The multiplier is strictly positive and bounded on the frozen domain. These empirical acceleration laws are not claimed to possess a stable covariant action until one is derived.
